stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Many immunologists have assumed that the strength of a vaccine's initial antibody response determines how long its protection lasts. Immunologist Rana Okafor, however, has found that durable protection depends instead on memory B cells that settle in the bone marrow, and that these cells form only when a vaccine's antigen remains in the lymph nodes for at least two weeks. Her team has also shown that an experimental slow-release formulation keeps antigen in the lymph nodes for about three weeks. Taken together, these findings suggest that the slow-release formulation ______
choices: will provide lasting protection to every person who receives it
meets a requirement for forming the memory cells tied to lasting protection
keeps antigen in the lymph nodes longer than any other formulation does
works chiefly by strengthening the vaccine's initial antibody response
explanation: The term the two facts share is antigen staying in the lymph nodes. The memory cells form only when antigen stays at least two weeks, and the formulation keeps it there about three weeks. So the formulation meets that condition. The word 'only' makes this a necessary condition, not a guarantee, so the most you can conclude is that the formulation meets a requirement.

A.why: You treated 'form only when' as if it meant 'always form when.' Meeting a necessary condition does not guarantee the result, and nothing in the text supports 'every person.'

C.why: You used only the fact about the formulation and stretched it into a comparison with all other formulations. The text never compares it with anything else.

D.why: You went back to the popular view that the passage undercuts. Okafor ties durability to memory B cells, not to the initial antibody response.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: In a four-year trial, agronomist Luis Ferreira planted winter rye between soybean seasons on half of a set of test plots. While the rye had no measurable effect on the following soybean yields, it substantially raised soil organic matter compared with the unplanted plots. Separate studies have established that soils richer in organic matter hold more water after rainfall. Taken together, these results suggest that planting winter rye between soybean seasons ______
choices: should help the soil retain more water after rainfall
should raise soybean yields by helping soil retain water
raises soil organic matter more than any other cover crop
should improve water retention in every soil and climate
explanation: The shared term is soil organic matter. Rye raises organic matter, and more organic matter means the soil holds more water. So rye should help the soil retain water. The yield result stayed the same, so the change you can infer is about water, not harvests.

B.why: You carried the chain into yields, but the passage says the rye had no measurable effect on soybean yields.

C.why: You took only the organic-matter fact and added a comparison with other cover crops. The trial tested only rye against unplanted plots.

D.why: You let 'every' slip past. One trial's plots cannot support a claim about all soils and climates.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Clinic case counts are a lagging measure of influenza's spread, because people typically seek care several days after they begin shedding the virus. Wastewater testing avoids this delay: infected people shed detectable viral material into sewage starting on roughly the first day of infection. This year, the city of Marlow began testing weekly samples from each of its sewage treatment plants. By adopting this approach, Marlow's health officials are likely able to ______
choices: prevent influenza from spreading among the city's residents
identify which individual residents have become infected
detect rising influenza infections before clinic counts show them
confirm influenza outbreaks only after clinics have reported them
explanation: The passage names the flaw in clinic counts, which is delay. It says wastewater picks up the virus from about the first day of infection, and that Marlow now tests wastewater. Linking these facts, Marlow can see rising infections earlier than clinic counts alone would show them.

A.why: You added an extra step. Detecting infections early might help officials respond, but the passage never says that detection stops the virus from spreading.

B.why: You assumed sewage samples can be traced to particular people. The passage describes pooled samples from treatment plants, not individual tests.

D.why: This reverses the point of the passage. Wastewater testing is described as a way to avoid waiting for clinic reports.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Seismologist Ines Varga studies slow slip events, episodes in which a fault moves gradually over weeks without producing strong shaking. Her models indicate that such events can shift stress onto neighboring locked sections of a fault, and earlier research has shown that added stress on a locked section increases the chance that it will rupture in a large earthquake. In 2023, GPS stations recorded a slow slip event beside a locked section of the offshore Kerran Fault. Varga's work therefore implies that the event ______
choices: will trigger a large earthquake on the locked section within weeks
released stress that had built up on the fault's locked section
made the Kerran Fault more hazardous than any other offshore fault
may have made a large earthquake on the locked section more likely
explanation: The shared term is stress on the locked section. Slow slip can add that stress, and added stress raises the chance of rupture. So the 2023 event may have raised the chance of a large earthquake. The words 'can' and 'chance' limit how strong the conclusion can be, which is why the answer says 'may have' and 'more likely.'

A.why: This is strength creep. The passage supports a higher chance of an earthquake, not a certain one within a set time.

B.why: You reversed the relationship. The passage says slow slip shifts stress onto locked sections, not that it relieves their stress.

C.why: You went past the chain with a comparison nobody made. The passage says nothing about other offshore faults.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: For centuries, printmakers etched their plates with nitric acid, which bites cleanly into metal but releases toxic nitrogen dioxide fumes that can damage the lungs of anyone working nearby. Ferric chloride, a salt solution, etches copper without giving off such fumes, although it works poorly on the zinc plates many printmakers favor. After years of using nitric acid on zinc, printmaker Hana Lindqvist switched to ferric chloride and began working only on copper plates. By making both changes, Lindqvist most likely ______
choices: avoided the harmful fumes while still being able to etch her plates
could keep etching the zinc plates she had used for years
made sharper prints than nitric acid would have allowed
eliminated every health risk involved in etching her plates
explanation: The passage gives two facts about ferric chloride: it releases no toxic fumes, and it works on copper but poorly on zinc. Lindqvist made two changes, switching to ferric chloride and to copper. Together they let her avoid the fumes and still etch her plates effectively.

B.why: You missed the qualification. Ferric chloride works poorly on zinc, which is why Lindqvist moved to copper.

C.why: You assumed the new method is better in quality. The passage compares the two methods only on fumes, not on how sharp the prints are.

D.why: You stretched 'avoids one hazard' into 'avoids every hazard.' The passage addresses only the nitrogen dioxide fumes.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Hydrologist Mara Quist compared streams in a semiarid basin before and after beavers were reintroduced. Although the beavers' dams did not change the total volume of water the streams carried over a year, they raised the nearby water table by as much as a meter. Earlier research had shown that in such basins, a higher water table releases groundwater into streams through the dry late-summer months. Quist's findings therefore suggest that beaver dams in the basin can ______
choices: increase the total amount of water the streams carry each year
raise the water table by a meter wherever beavers are introduced
help the streams keep flowing through the dry late-summer months
reduce how much groundwater the streams receive in late summer
explanation: The shared term is the water table. The dams raise it, and a higher water table feeds groundwater into streams in late summer. So the dams can help the streams keep flowing in the dry months. Annual volume did not change, so the effect you can infer is about timing, not total amount.

A.why: You picked the result that did not change. The passage says the dams did not change the total annual volume.

B.why: You used only the water-table fact and applied it to every place beavers live. The study covered one basin, and 'as much as a meter' is a maximum, not a typical figure.

D.why: You reversed the chain. A higher water table releases more groundwater into streams, not less.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Because of its unusually adventurous harmonies, Friedrich Aldermann's String Quartet in E-flat has long been assumed to date from the final years of his life, around 1805. Musicologist Beatriz Llorente, however, points out that the only surviving manuscript of the quartet, written in Aldermann's own hand, is on paper from the Hollern mill. Aldermann's letters and dated scores show that he used Hollern paper only from 1776 to 1780, while he lived in Vienna. Llorente's evidence therefore suggests that the quartet ______
choices: was the final piece Aldermann completed before he left Vienna
was likely written during Aldermann's Vienna years, not late in life
was composed around 1805 on paper Aldermann had saved from Vienna
shows that adventurous harmony was typical of all Viennese composers
explanation: Link the facts through the Hollern paper. The manuscript in Aldermann's hand is on Hollern paper, and he used that paper only from 1776 to 1780 in Vienna. So he probably wrote the quartet during those years. The 'however' tells you the blank finishes Llorente's corrected view, not the old assumption.

A.why: You added more precision than the evidence gives. The paper puts the quartet somewhere in 1776–1780, not at the end of his time in Vienna.

C.why: You held on to the popular view that the passage undercuts. Aldermann's records show he used Hollern paper only until 1780, so this answer needs an assumption the passage contradicts.

D.why: You went past the chain to a claim about all Viennese composers. The evidence is about when one quartet was written, not about a whole group's style.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Chemical analysis of a fourteenth-century wool fragment dyed in the town of Serro revealed alizarin, a red dye compound that in medieval Europe came only from the roots of the madder plant. The analysis also found aluminum residue left by alum, a mineral salt used to bind dye to fibers. Tax records show that throughout the fourteenth century, all alum reaching Serro was imported from mines in Anatolia. The dyers who colored the fragment therefore ______
choices: grew their madder in fields near the Anatolian alum mines
used madder because alum could not be obtained in Serro
produced a redder wool than any other medieval European dyers
combined madder with alum that had come from Anatolian mines
explanation: You need three facts together. Alizarin means the dyers used madder. The aluminum residue means they used alum. All alum in Serro came from Anatolia. So they combined madder with Anatolian alum. Each part of the answer comes directly from a stated fact.

A.why: You added an extra step. The passage says where the alum came from, not where the madder was grown.

B.why: The fragment contains alum residue, and the tax records show that alum reached Serro, so alum was available there.

C.why: You went past the chain to a comparison with all other European dyers. The analysis describes only one fragment.
